market_holds: Spot $10.64 at the 2026-11-24 close (sealed baseline), 2.4% above the 52-week low and 46.9% below the high. Run-up -8.0% over 5 days and -5.5% over 20 days. Front-expiry straddle 6.77%, event-implied 5.95% (indicative only: the ATM spread is 67% of mid). Skew is +12.6 vol points toward puts, so the market pays for downside. Measured from the Yahoo bars in my work dir, the slide since 2026-11-06 is mostly the sector and the tape: LI 12.53 to 10.67 (-15%), NIO -24%, XPEV -12% (after a guide beat), KWEB -15%. On 11-20 LI fell 7.6% alongside XPEV -13.9% and NIO -7.9%, and I found no LI-specific news for that day. Consensus on the quarter: Earnings Whispers (2026-11-18) has EPS -$0.08 and revenue about $4.09bn, near the top of the RMB26.6-28.0bn guide, so deliveries of 99,964 at the top of guidance are already in it. Deutsche Bank (2026-11-10) has a net loss of RMB0.3bn and gross margin of 16.7% (Q2: 11.0%), against a Bloomberg consensus loss of RMB942m that it cites. The DB note also covers November above 40k including 16-20k i6, i6 orders above 50k, and a 9-11 week i6 wait. I found no published Q4 delivery or revenue consensus. Last reactions, close to close from Yahoo daily bars: Q2'26 on 2026-08-26 -1.1% after a Q3 revenue guide of RMB26.6-28bn against a RMB32.3bn consensus; Q1'26 on 2026-05-28 -1.5% (open -4.7%); Q3'25 on 2025-11-26 +0.6% (open -2.0%) after a Q4 guide about 23% below consensus; Q2'25 +2.9%; Q1'25 +2.1%; Q4'24 -4.4%. So three straight guides came in below consensus and the stock moved only 1-5% each time.
view: The stock trades on the next-quarter delivery and revenue guide, and secondly on vehicle margin. Q3 itself is largely known: deliveries landed at the top of guidance and consensus revenue already sits at the top of the range. The margin recovery has been previewed publicly (DB 16.7% GM). Whether it beats depends on which consensus is the bar: DB's RMB942m Bloomberg loss would be beaten, while EW's -$0.08 is closer to a mid-teens margin. For Q4 the visible inputs are October at 29,025, the weakest month since February, plus the i6 changeover. Against that, the refreshed i6 has 20k/month capacity in November rising in December, a dealer-checked backlog above 50k orders and 9-11 week waits. That points to a Q4 guide around 115-130k, above Q4'25's 109k. Against that: insurance subsidies on mature L-series models were doubled to RMB10k, the L9/L8/i8 have no wait (soft EREV demand), there is a Mega screen shortage, and management has guided below the street three times running. I cannot see the street's Q4 number, so I cannot say which side of it the guide lands. The 15% slide since 11-06 came with the sector and China tech, not with LI news, so it lowers the bar without telling me the release clears it. The market cap sits roughly at the cash balance (RMB87.5bn at 6-30, about $13bn). That, the muted history of reactions to bad guides and the downside skew suggest a miss moves the stock less than a good guide plus a margin beat would. That argues for a slight up tilt and a move smaller than implied, not a confident direction.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is the Q4 delivery/revenue guide, and I found no Q4 consensus to set the i6 ramp evidence (above 50k orders, 20k/month capacity, DB November above 40k) against. That evidence is public and dated before the stock's sector-driven slide. Margin recovery is previewed and probably partly expected. Nothing here gets me to 65% on either side.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 delivery guide at or above roughly 125k with Q3 vehicle margin in the mid-teens would make the up side clearly more likely. A guide near Q4'25's 109k, or a vehicle margin still near 10%, would make the down side more likely.

self_critique: Management has guided below consensus three quarters running, and the L-series EREV core is visibly soft (doubled subsidies, no wait times, October the weakest since February). A cautious Q4 guide, for example 110-120k, with a heavy loss outlook could take the stock to new lows despite the cheap valuation, since the skew already says the market fears that. On the other side, the cash cushion and muted reaction history may make the stock move less than I assume in either direction. Both cases keep me near 50.
approach_notes: P6's decomposition of the run-in (peers and KWEB beside LI) was the most useful step and stopped me from reading the 15% slide as company news. P7's push to estimate the line from its inputs was hard to apply without any visible Q4 consensus. A route to a stale street Q4 number (e.g. the delivery-estimate tables in HK broker notes) would be the decisive input.
